◆ tommy_malloc

#define tommy_malloc   malloc

Generic malloc(), calloc(), realloc() and free() functions.

Redefine them to what you need. By default they map to the C malloc(), calloc(), realloc() and free().

Infallible Allocation Invariant
Tommy assumes that dynamic memory allocation never fails and that these functions always return a valid, non-zero pointer. The library does not check for allocation failures and does not return error codes for out-of-memory (OOM) conditions.
Rationale
This choice reflects the memory model of modern general-purpose operating systems:
  • Virtual Memory Overcommit: On modern systems (such as Linux with default overcommit heuristics), malloc() reserves virtual address space and almost never returns 0 on 64-bit systems. Physical memory is committed on first write, meaning actual exhaustion triggers the kernel OOM Killer (SIGKILL) rather than an allocation failure. Checking for null returns in userspace often provides a false sense of security.
  • Swap Thrashing: In systems backed by swap, severe memory pressure causes destructive disk thrashing, degrading throughput by orders of magnitude and rendering the process unusable long before an allocation call fails.
Advantages
  • Zero Error-Path Overhead: No branch predictions, conditional jumps, or status checks inside critical insertion and resizing loops, maximizing CPU cache efficiency and execution speed.
  • Clean and Lean API: Functions (such as insertion and resizing) can remain simple (often returning void or direct element pointers) without cluttering client code with error-propagation boilerplate.
  • Deterministic Consistency: Avoids complex transactional rollback logic otherwise required if an allocation failed halfway through dynamic table growth or node migration.
  • Industry Alignment: Follows the established design of high-performance systems libraries (e.g., GLib's g_malloc, Git's xmalloc, Redis's zmalloc, and default C++ operator new).
Trade-offs and Limitations
  • Embedded and Bare-Metal Systems: Systems without an MMU/virtual memory (e.g., RTOS, microcontrollers) or strict overcommit disabled (vm.overcommit_memory=2) do return 0 on heap exhaustion.
  • Multi-Tenant Services: Infrastructure daemons (e.g., database engines) that must isolate a single client's excessive memory request without crashing the entire process cannot rely on unchecked allocations.
Custom Interception
If your environment requires custom handling (such as memory tracking, structured aborts, or logging), redefine tommy_malloc, tommy_calloc, tommy_realloc, and tommy_free before including Tommy headers (or via compiler flags). Custom allocators must terminate the process (e.g., abort()) or initiate an unwinding non-local exit (e.g., longjmp or C++ exception) rather than returning 0.

◆ tommy_uint_t

typedef tommy_uint32_t tommy_uint_t

Generic unsigned integer type.

It has no specific size, as it is used to store only small values. To make the code more efficient, a full 32-bit integer is used.

◆ tommy_node

typedef struct tommy_node_struct tommy_node

Data structure node.

This node type is shared between all the data structures and used to store some info directly into the elements you want to store.

A typical declaration is:

struct element {
tommy_node node;
// other fields
};

◆ tommy_compare_func

typedef int tommy_compare_func(const void *elem_a, const void *elem_b)

Compare function for elements.

This function is like the C strcmp().

struct element {
tommy_node node;
int value;
};
int compare(const void* elem_a, const void* elem_b)
{
if (((const struct element*)elem_a)->value < ((const struct element*)elem_b)->value)
return -1;
if (((const struct element*)elem_a)->value > ((const struct element*)elem_b)->value)
return 1;
return 0;
}
tommy_list_sort(&list, compare);
tommy_list_sort
TOMMY_API void tommy_list_sort(tommy_list *list, tommy_compare_func *cmp)
Sorts a list.
Parameters
elem_aPointer to the first element to compare.
elem_bPointer to the second element to compare.
Returns
<0 if the first element is less than the second, ==0 if equal, >0 if greater.

typedef int tommy_search_func(const void *arg, const void *elem)

Search function for elements.

struct element {
tommy_node node;
int value;
};
int compare(const void* arg, const void* elem)
{
const int* value_to_find = arg;
const struct element* element_to_compare = elem;
return *value_to_find != element_to_compare->value;
}
int value_to_find = 1;
struct element* elem = tommy_hashtable_search(&hashtable, compare, &value_to_find, tommy_inthash_u32(value_to_find));
if (!elem) {
// not found
} else {
// found
}

◆ tommy_ilog2_u32()

tommy_uint_t tommy_ilog2_u32 ( tommy_uint32_t  value)

Bit scan reverse or integer log2.

Return the bit index of the most significant 1 bit.

If no bit is set, the result is undefined. To force a return 0 in this case, you can use tommy_ilog2_u32(value | 1).

Other interesting ways for bitscan are at:

Bit Twiddling Hacks http://graphics.stanford.edu/~seander/bithacks.html

Chess Programming BitScan http://chessprogramming.wikispaces.com/BitScan

Parameters
valueValue to scan. 0 is not allowed.
Returns
The index of the most significant bit set.
